title: US STOCKS-S&P flat as tech boost offsets Turkish currency worries
text:
Shutterstock photo US STOCKS-S&P flat as tech boost offsets Turkish currency worries
* Nielsen jumps after activist investor pushes for sale
* Tech stocks gain the most among S&P sectors
* Apple and Amazon hit record highs
* Indexes: Dow down 0.17 pct, S&P up 0.03, Nasdaq up 0.20pct
* Graphic: World FX rates in 2018 https://reut.rs/2vFv6Ue (Changes comment, adds details, updates prices)
By Amy Caren Daniel
Aug 13 (Reuters) - The S&P 500 index treaded water on Mondayas high-flying companies such as Apple and Amazon hit recordhighs, offsetting declines in shares of U.S. lenders due to aplunge in Turkish lira.
The technology sector .SPLRCT rose 0.43 percent and wasthe top gainer among the major S&P sectors.
Apple's shares AAPL.O jumped as much as 1.6 percent to hita record high of $210.95 and Amazon.comAMZN.O rose as much as2.1 percent to an all-time high of $1,925.00, whileGoogle-parent Alphabet GOOGL.O gained 0.2 percent.
"We have returned to a market based on fundamentals," saidEd Cofrancesco, president and chief executive officer atInternational Assets Advisory in Orlando, Florida.
"When we have a growing market, tech stocks are going to dowell and this is a sign that the economy is doing well and willcontinue to do so."
The financials .SPSY slipped 0.3 percent as U.S. bankstocks, like its European counterparts, bore the brunt ofinvestor worries over exposure to Turkey's crisis.
Shares of CitigroupC.N , Bank of AmericaBAC.N , WellsFargo WFC.N and JP Morgan JPM.N were down between 0.3percent and 0.5 percent.
The lira TRY= has tumbled more than 40 percent https://reut.rs/2vFv6Ue against the dollar this year on worries over President TayyipErdogan's increasing control over the economy and deterioratingrelations with the United States. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL5N1V407X
At 11:23 a.m. EDT the Dow Jones Industrial Average .DJI was down 42.08 points, or 0.17 percent, at 25,271.06, the S&P500 .SPX was up 0.77 points, or 0.03 percent, at 2,834.05 andthe Nasdaq Composite .IXIC was up 15.93 points, or 0.20percent, at 7,855.04.
Among stocks, Harley DavidsonHOG.N fell 3 percent afterPresident Donald Trump backed boycotting American motorcyclemanufacturer. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL1N1V303F
Netflix's shares dipped 0.6 percent and was the only one ofthe FAANG stocks trading lower, after the video streamingservice provider said its Chief Financial Officer David Wellsplans to step down. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL4N1V44RW
Nielsen HoldingsNLSN.N jumped 9.6 percent, the most onthe S&P 500, after activist investor Elliott Managementdisclosed a stake and said would push for a sale of theTV-ratings company. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL4N1V44IW
VF CorpVFC.N dropped 4.6 percent and was the biggest dragon the S&P after the apparel maker decided to spin off Lee andWrangler jeans into a separate public company. urn:newsml:reuters.com:*:nL4N1V43SU
Declining issues outnumbered advancers for a 1.45-to-1 ratioon the NYSE and for a 1.32-to-1 ratio on the Nasdaq.
The S&P index recorded 11 new 52-week highs and six newlows, while the Nasdaq recorded 49 new highs and 74 new lows.
